chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali Al-Zaytuni and others, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Hamzah, from 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), both said:

Whoever wishes for one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand prophets to shake his hand, let him visit the grave of Abi 'Abdillah Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him) on the fifteenth of Sha'ban. Verily, the souls of the prophets (peace be upon them) ask permission from Allah to visit him, and permission is granted to them. Among them are five: the Ulul 'Azm (Prophs of Determination) from the Messengers. We asked, 'Who are they?' He said, 'Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, 'Isa, and Muhammad (peace be upon them all).' We asked him, 'What is the meaning of Ulul 'Azm?' He said, 'They were sent to the east and west of the earth, to its jinn and its humans.'

key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Al-Husayn's grave on the 15th of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the cosmic significance of the 15th of Sha'ban by linking the intercession of the five Ulul 'Azm prophets to the spiritual elevation of the visitor. It defines Ulul 'Azm not merely by their rank but by their universal mission to both humans and jinn, reinforcing the comprehensive scope of Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) authority in the afterlife.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Zaytūni, and from others, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ḥamzah, who said: ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (Imam Sajjād (a.s.)) said:

Those who would like one hundred and twenty-four thousand prophets to shake their hand, should go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh, Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.), on the fifteenth of Sha’bān. Verily the souls of the prophets (a.s.), including the five ULUL ‘AZM Messengers, ask permission from Allāh (on that day) to go to his Ziyārah and they will be granted permission. We asked, “Who are the five Ulul ‘Azm (prophets)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Nūḥ, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, ‘Isā (a.s.), and Muḥammad (s.a.a.w.).” We asked, “What does Ulul ‘Azm mean?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “They (are the prophets who) were sent to the east and the west of the earth and to (all of) Jinn and mankind.” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father and all of my scholars, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali Al-Zaytūni, and from others, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Uthmān, from Abī Basīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)).
